description.narrative: This project aims to contribute to a sustainable and inclusive cocoa value chain, in which producers receive fair value for their produce and work under safe conditions, without the use of child labour, and land rights and forest are protected.

title.narrative: # of individuals activated and mobilized to raise their voice to push the policy agenda, influence societal (gender) norms, make informed decisions (consumer and corporate behaviour, e.g. on production and consumption practices)

comment.narrative: 249 individuals (3 continue, 246 new) from 83 Co-ops. In 5 regions mobilsed and activated to raise voices on cocoa price, cocoa smuggling, cocoa farmland destruction and push child labour agenda

3 individuals from cooperatives (BAWCOF and Sefwi Bekwai farmers union) were activated and continued to push the agenda of spousal rights in land. And push the agenda of land documentation for cocoa farmers.

comment.narrative:
-dialogue on tree tenure -dialogue on sector investment coordination -EU cocoa talk on child labor -EU cocoa dialogue on deforestation
During the last quarter of the year, the RMSC of the FC called for stakeholder dilaouge to validate the tree tenure registration form which aims to address issues of forest degradation and the cutting down of trees by farmers. We support Elluokrom cocoa farmers association to participate in this dialogue.
In addition SWA particiipated in the EU cocoa talk on defoestation and key recommendations in clude zoning and landscape management planning, stakeholders to preserve high carbon stock (HCS) and high carbon value areas, even in ?off-reserve? landscapes. Cocoa Management System to open up the system for stakeholder participation, to enhance trust and improve the credibility of the system
We participated in the EU-Ghana cocoa dialogues that focuses specifically on childlabour and forces labor in the cocos supply chain. Solidaridad joined other CSOs (GCCP) to make a presentation on childlbabor in the cocoa sector. We reviewed and contributed to that presentation.

Dialogue participated Transformative Land Investment Land sector Multi-stakeholder platform Dialogue convened/initiated Tree tenure dialogue Dialogue on cocoa price 6 Co-op. CSOs and cocobod Dialogue with Doc to form Co-op. Assoc.

a district dialogue with the chief, queen mothers, and farmers on cocoa land documentation, a dialogue with cocoa cooperatives to form a uniformed body to advocate for better representation. A dialogue with TWG on national land conference. This led to the establishment of MSP on land during the conference, a dialogue on child labor with GCCP

title.narrative: # of (governmental and private) policies for sustainable production, trade and consumption influenced

comment.narrative: 2 policies were effectively influenced. These are the Land act 2020 and the Ghana children act 1998, ie. child labor
Tree ownership, Cocoa Price policy and the Ghana Children Act were successfully influenced
